title: Chapter 12
content:
Clack.

Another pebble skittered across the dirt, joining the small mound piled beneath the brick wall. Crouched on the curb, young Jakyeong reached down with grubby fingers, repeatedly scooping up loose stones and hurling them at the base of the fence.

His sneakers were worn down to the threadbare insoles. His trousers, outgrown by a couple of inches, left his bare ankles bitten raw by the winter wind, and the frayed cuffs of his hand-me-down jacket offered little defense against the cold.

As he tossed another stone, a cluster of neighborhood children walking by with backpacks began whispering amongst themselves. The second Jakyeong's eyes met theirs, they shrieked in fright and scrambled away.

The little ghost.

That was what the neighborhood kids called him—a nickname born from the fact that his family only ever seemed to stir under the cover of night.

"What are you doing out here?"

An iron gate creaked open from the compound wall, and a tall man stepped out. Seeing the miniature mountain of pebbles piled against his brickwork, the man didn't scold the boy. Instead, he slipped back inside for a moment and returned with a fresh pastry.

He was a Chinese national who had lived in the neighborhood long before Jakyeong’s family drifted into the slums. He had a son older than Jakyeong, who was currently living in China with his mother and grandmother.

Taking the pastry, Jakyeong ripped the wrapper open with his teeth and shoved it into his mouth, ravenous. Whenever he loitered around this corner long enough, the man would come out to slip him something to eat. Most of the time it was bread or pastries, but on a few rare occasions, he’d brought Jakyeong inside to cook him a hot bowl of ramen. Every time that happened, though, Jakyeong’s father would fly into a violent fury, screaming that the dirty foreigner was trying to groom his son.

"Slow down. You'll choke," the man said softly.

Jakyeong hadn't eaten since yesterday. He’d rummaged through the fridge that morning, but it was barren. His father had gone out on a job three days ago and hadn't returned, and his mother had been passed out cold for days, pickled in a haze of cheap liquor and narcotics.

"What a miserable lot in life you were dealt, kid..."

The man—whose surname was Wang—pulled a cigarette from his pack, placed it between his lips, and sparked the tip. A thick ribbon of pale smoke drifted up into the freezing air. Swallowing the last bite of bread, Jakyeong stared blankly at the burning cherry in the man's mouth.

"What? Want a drag?" Mr. Wang asked with a dry chuckle.

Jakyeong nodded.

The man's narrow eyes widened slightly, then softened. After a beat of hesitation, he waved Jakyeong over, offering the filtered end to the boy’s mouth.

"Draw it in deep and swallow."

Pursing his lips around the filter, Jakyeong sucked in hard just as he was told.

Instantly, a violent fit of hacking coughs tore from his chest. His eyes stung with tears, his throat burning as if he’d swallowed hot coals. Above him, a deep, hearty laugh rumbled through the cold, followed by a heavy hand affectionately ruffling his matted hair.

"See that? Nothing good comes from these damn things."

Watching the man's warm, easy smile, Jakyeong caught himself wishing—just for a fleeting second—that this man was his father. And in the same breath, he felt a bitter pang of jealousy toward the son living safely across the sea in China.

When Mr. Wang finished his smoke and headed back inside, Jakyeong turned and began trudging up the hill toward his own house.

His home sat at the very peak of the shantytown. The climb required navigating a dizzyingly steep concrete stairway—a treacherous drop where a single misstep meant plunging to your death. Just last winter, an elderly neighbor had slipped on the ice, tumbling down the flight until his neck snapped on the landing.

With every step closer to the summit, Jakyeong’s chest grew heavier. Pushing open the peeling, rusted iron gate, strange sounds leaked from inside the cramped house.

He froze at the threshold. Resting beneath the weathered wooden porch was a pair of men's shoes he didn't recognize.

A visitor.

"Ah, mm... Ah! Harder... suck it harder, oppa..."

"Haah... you filthy fucking bitch. You like that? Huh? Am I better than your useless husband?"

Jakyeong sat down on the edge of the porch as if nothing were amiss, casually kicking the dirt with the worn toes of his sneakers. Thump. Thump.

Inside, his mother’s frantic, breathy cries reached a crescendo, followed by a low, guttural grunt from the man. Then, only the heavy, ragged sound of two people catching their breath.

Did I eat that pastry too fast?

A wave of nausea twisted in Jakyeong's gut. As he rubbed his stomach, the flimsy wooden door banged open with enough force to rattle the frame, and a man stepped out into the yard.

Fastening his belt, the man’s face was one Jakyeong had seen a few times before.

"Hey. Your brat's sitting out here."

The man reached down to touch Jakyeong’s head, but the boy recoiled, pulling his torso back with undisguised disgust. The man let out a scoffing chuckle, pulling a cigarette from his pocket.

Tattooed across the man's bare shoulder was the grotesque, snarling face of a dokkaebi goblin.

It had four distinct horns—two protruding from its forehead and two jutting from its jaw—and glowing crimson eyes that seemed to glare straight into Jakyeong's soul. The boy averted his gaze immediately.

THWACK.

A sudden blow struck the back of Jakyeong’s skull. His small body pitched forward violently from the impact.

"Where the fuck have you been crawling around all morning?!"

When he didn't answer, a hard palm cracked across his face. Blood splattered from his nose, dripping onto the dirt. Jakyeong wiped the crimson smear across his sleeve, glaring up at his mother.

Pulling her robe tight to conceal an exposed breast, she accepted a lit cigarette from the man.

The man snickered, tossing a filthy floor rag toward Jakyeong. "Wipe yourself up."

Instead of taking the rag, Jakyeong kept his eyes locked on the man in a cold, venomous glare. The man seemed indifferent, but his mother snapped, screaming that she hated the disrespectful look in his eyes before kicking him square in the ribs.

His frail, stick-thin body went rolling across the gravel yard.

Lying in the dirt, all that filled Jakyeong’s vision was an impossibly, mercilessly blue sky. The harsh sunlight burned his eyes. If tears threatened to spill from his lashes, he told himself it was entirely the sky's fault.

"You alright there?"

Meeting Choi Ki-tae’s gaze, Jakyeong shook the long-buried memory from his head, curving his lips into a soft, docile smile as he nodded.

The mugger who had held a knife to his ribs had already fled into the shadows after receiving a savage, bloody beating and stammering out frantic apologies. Now, only the man with the goblin tattoo remained standing in the alley.

"Seok-joo’s in no shape to drive you back, so he asked me to step in," Ki-tae said, rolling down his sleeve. "Lucky I stepped out when I did, or things could've gotten ugly."

"I can just catch a cab, thank you," Jakyeong murmured, bowing politely and turning to leave.

Ki-tae’s hand clamped down on his bicep. Jakyeong’s eyes flicked once more to the ink resting beneath the fabric.

"Any friend of Seok-joo is a friend of mine. I'll drive you."

"I appreciate the offer, but really, I can manage on my own..."

"Look, it’s a pain in the ass for me too, but I don't have a choice," Ki-tae said, his sharp eyes narrowing into a playful yet lethal crescent. "If anything happens to you on my watch, it won't just be Seok-joo who gets skinned alive—every single person in that club tonight is a dead man. Literally dead. I don't need to spell out who I'm talking about, do I?"

He was obviously referring to Kang Il-hyun.

Realizing that pushing the issue would only raise red flags, Jakyeong conceded quickly. Ki-tae gestured for him to follow and led the way toward the main street. Judging by his steady stride, the man hadn't touched any alcohol or narcotics tonight.

Parked in front of the club was a sleek white sports car. A valet held the passenger door open, and Jakyeong slid inside, fastening his seatbelt.

Looking over, he realized the passenger seat was reclined almost flat. As he fumbled around the center console searching for the adjustment lever, Ki-tae slid into the driver's seat, leaning his entire upper body across the console to reach the button for him.

The sudden movement brought them chest-to-chest, Ki-tae’s mouth hovering inches from Jakyeong’s ear. A heavy cloud of musky cologne washed over him.

"Sorry about that," Ki-tae murmured smoothly. "Had a little fun in here earlier today."

"..."

"Sex, I mean."

Straightening back up into his seat, Ki-tae flashed a sly grin. "Ever done it in a car?"

Jakyeong shook his head meekly. Ki-tae let out an amused chuckle, muttering that he figured as much.

The engine roared to life, and the sports car peeled out of the narrow slum, merging into the wide avenues of the city. Despite the late hour, the expressway was bustling with traffic. Throughout the drive, Ki-tae kept throwing casual glances across the console.

"Heard you flew in from Hong Kong."

"Yes..."

"Your Korean is remarkably clean."

"My mother is Korean."

"Ah, so you're mixed?"

"Yes."

For the majority of the ride, Ki-tae threw out leading questions while Jakyeong kept his answers minimal, offering soft nods and polite one-word replies.

As the conversation tapered off, the sports car pulled up to a red light. Feeling the weight of mental fatigue, Jakyeong slipped off his horn-rimmed glasses and rubbed his eyes. When he looked back up, he caught Ki-tae staring directly at him, his thumb slowly stroking his own bottom lip.

"If I had a face like that," Ki-tae murmured, "I sure as hell wouldn't hide it behind glasses."

Jakyeong put the frames back on without a word.

"You remember that girl sitting next to you earlier?" Ki-tae continued. "She's a top commercial model right now. Father’s a massive heavyweight, too."

Jakyeong recalled the half-naked girl who had brazenly groped him on the lounge sofa.

"Most guys would kill to have a girl like that throw herself at them. Guess your standards are through the roof... or do you prefer guys?"

The light turned green, and the car accelerated forward.

Jakyeong shook his head firmly. "No, sir."

He knew exactly what the man was fishing for. The predatory undertones had been obvious ever since Ki-tae leaned across his lap to adjust the seat. But having dealt with every stripe of degenerate in the underworld, Jakyeong wasn't rattled. He simply chalked it up to Wang Han’s old observation: his face had a habit of attracting dangerous attention from men and women alike.

Brushing off the occasional probing comment with vague hums and docile answers, the car finally approached the secluded mountain estate. As Kang Il-hyun’s residence loomed in the distance, the easy swagger on Ki-tae’s face tightened into visible unease.

Pulling up outside the massive iron gates, Ki-tae peered through the windshield at the illuminated compound. Two armed security guards were already descending the exterior stone steps to inspect the unfamiliar vehicle.

"Building a fortress out in the middle of nowhere... Guy's an eccentric freak, isn't he?"

"Thank you for the ride. Get home safely," Jakyeong said, reaching for the door handle.

Before he could push it open, Ki-tae caught his forearm. Pulling a sleek black business card from his leather wallet, he pressed it into Jakyeong’s palm. The card contained nothing but a single, private phone number embossed in silver.

"My personal line," Ki-tae said, locking eyes with him. "I don't hand this out to just anyone, so keep it close."

Jakyeong looked down at the card, then met Ki-tae’s gaze.

"If you ever need anything... hit me up. I'll give you a steep discount."

A discount on what? Narcotics? Or your body?

Knowing that refusing would only prolong the encounter, Jakyeong pocketed the card. But just as he pushed the car door open, he froze.

Standing right past the perimeter gate was a tall, imposing silhouette.

The moment Ki-tae recognized Kang Il-hyun, a quiet curse slipped through his teeth. In a flash, he scrambled out of the sports car, rushing around to the gate and bowing so low his forehead practically grazed the asphalt.

"Good evening, Executive Director Kang!"

The smug, predatory swagger from the car ride was completely incinerated.

Stepping out a moment later, Jakyeong offered a subtle, polite nod.

Kang Il-hyun stood beneath the gate lights with a cigarette dangling between his lips. Even shrouded in the dark, the look in his eyes as he stared down at Choi Ki-tae was lethal. Sensing the suffocating pressure, Ki-tae stood trembling in place.

Instead of acknowledging the greeting and heading inside, Il-hyun shoved his hands into his slacks and slowly descended the stone steps. The quiet, unhurried cadence of his footsteps carried an overwhelming menace.

Stopping right in front of Jakyeong, Il-hyun held out an open palm.

"Give me what he just handed you."

Jakyeong’s eyes widened a fraction behind his lenses. The windows were heavily tinted. How did he catch that?

Reading the icy detachment in Il-hyun's face, Jakyeong decided compliance was the wisest move. Reaching into his trousers, he pulled out the card and placed it into Il-hyun’s palm.

Il-hyun caught the card between his index and middle fingers, then slowly turned his head toward Ki-tae. Under that piercing, pit-viper gaze, Ki-tae cowered, his head sinking lower into his shoulders.

"Hey, kid."

"Y-Yes, sir..."

Flick.

With a sharp snap of Il-hyun's fingers, the stiff card spun through the air, smacking hard against Ki-tae’s cheek before fluttering into the dirt.

"Don't try pushing your garbage onto my guests," Il-hyun said, his voice dropping to a terrifying, quiet purr. "Or I'll have to teach you a lesson."

Despite the blatant humiliation, Ki-tae didn't dare offer an excuse. "I'm sorry, sir! My deepest apologies!"

Apparently unsatisfied with words alone, Il-hyun took the glowing cigarette from his lips and pressed the burning cherry directly into Ki-tae’s chest.

A sharp wisp of gray smoke hissed into the air as the ember burned clean through the thin cotton tee, sizzling straight into the flesh beneath.

Ki-tae’s jaw clamped shut, his brow contorting in agony, but he didn't dare flinch away.

Tossing the spent butt into the gravel, Il-hyun turned on his heel and strode back toward the gates without looking back.

Jakyeong didn't wait a second longer, quickly falling into step behind him.

Translator's Notes (A/N):

  • Daldongne / Moon Villages (골목 제일 위): Jakyeong's childhood flashback takes place in a classic Korean hillside shantytown (commonly called daldongne or "moon villages" because they sit so high up the steep hills they are close to the moon). These impoverished areas are notorious for dangerous, crumbling concrete stairways and extreme isolation.

  • Ethnic Slurs & Tension (짱깨): Jakyeong's father used the derogatory Korean slur jjang-kkae against their Chinese neighbor, highlighting the xenophobic underbelly of the slums and contrasting Mr. Wang's genuine paternal kindness with Jakyeong's abusive biological family.

  • Dokkaebi Horns (뿔 넷 달린 도깨비): Traditional Korean dokkaebi tattoos usually feature one or two horns. A four-horned design (two on the forehead, two on the jaw) with crimson eyes is a highly specific, sinister underworld calling card that connects Ki-tae directly to the man who abused Jakyeong's mother years ago.
